relationships.evidence: Jaguar Tooth is deployed via an SNMP exploit which grants remote code execution and write-access to the target operating system.
Jaguar Tooth exfiltrates collected device information over TFTP.
Jaguar Tooth patches the system image in memory to enable a user authentication bypass.
Jaguar Tooth patches two authentication functions to grant access to local accounts for Telnet and physical sessions, without checking the provided password.
Jaguar Tooth utilises a Cisco IOS CLI command to dump the current device running configuration.
Jaguar Tooth performs remote system discovery by utilising Cisco IOS CLI commands to obtain ARP and connected devices information.
Jaguar Tooth enumerates the local flash filesystem by utilising a Cisco IOS CLI command.
Jaguar Tooth utilises several Cisco IOS CLI commands to discover the system network configuration.
Jaguar Tooth discovers system information such as interfaces and software versioning by utilising several Cisco IOS CLI commands.
